pill.desc: clear, colorless to pale yellow solution in a single-dose prefilled pen

tell: An siRNA that lowers antithrombin, given every one or two months and carrying a boxed warning on thrombosis.

clues.text: In vitro, about 96.6% is bound to plasma proteins. It is broken down by endo- and exonucleases rather than CYP450 enzymes, with 14.6% of the dose recovered unchanged in urine.
A double-stranded nucleic acid carrying a triantennary N-acetylgalactosamine ligand. It is freely soluble in water, with a molecular weight of 17,193 daltons.
Approved under an NDA as 20 mg/0.2 mL vials and 50 mg/0.5 mL prefilled pens, dosed once a month or once every two months.
Boxed warning for thrombotic events and acute and recurrent gallbladder disease. No contraindications; viral infection and nasopharyngitis are the most common reactions.
Routine prophylaxis against bleeding episodes in patients aged 12 years and older with hemophilia A or B, with or without inhibitors.
A double-stranded siRNA that degrades antithrombin messenger RNA through RNA interference, lowering plasma antithrombin levels.
The generic name begins with F and has nine letters.
